title: “Monks, for a monk, those defilements that should be abandoned by direct knowledge have been abandoned by direct knowledge; those defilements that should be abandoned…
content: “Monks, for a monk, those defilements that should be abandoned by direct knowledge have been abandoned by direct knowledge; those defilements that should be abandoned by restraint have been abandoned by restraint … That monk is called one who lives restrained by the restraint of all defilements, who has cut off craving, has shed the fetters, has rightly penetrated conceit, and has made an end of suffering.”

title: “Monks, for an untaught ordinary person, contacted by feeling born of contact with ignorance, craving arises. From that craving, volitional formation arises. Thus, monks, that…
content: “Monks, for an untaught ordinary person, contacted by feeling born of contact with ignorance, craving arises. From that craving, volitional formation arises. Thus, monks, that formation is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen. That craving is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen. That feeling is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen. That contact is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen. That ignorance is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen. Monks, knowing thus, seeing thus, the defilements are immediately destroyed.”

title: “Monks, defilement is a disease; defilement is a boil; defilement is a dart. Therefore, monks, the Tathāgata dwells without defilement, free from the dart. Therefore,…
content: “Monks, defilement is a disease; defilement is a boil; defilement is a dart. Therefore, monks, the Tathāgata dwells without defilement, free from the dart. Therefore, monks, if any monk has a wish, let him wish to dwell without defilement, free from the dart. Do not conceive about the eye, do not conceive in the eye, do not conceive from the eye, do not conceive ‘the eye is mine.’ Do not conceive about forms … Do not conceive about eye-consciousness … Do not conceive about eye-contact … Whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact … do not conceive about that feeling, do not conceive in it, do not conceive from it, do not conceive ‘that feeling is mine.’ Not conceiving thus, he does not cling to anything in the world. Not clinging, he is not agitated. Not agitated, he personally attains Nibbāna. He knows: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’”

title: Craving for beautiful things, Delighting in agreeable forms, Bound by ignorance, Lowly beings Increase their bondage. Even the wise who do unwholesome deeds Born from…
content:
Craving for beautiful things,
Delighting in agreeable forms,
Bound by ignorance,
Lowly beings
Increase their bondage.
Even the wise who do unwholesome deeds
Born from greed, hatred, delusion —
Causing distress, discomfort,
Giving rise to suffering —
Are surrounded by ignorance,
Blind, without eyes.
Such is their nature —
They cannot think:
I can be thus.
